items.title: Lenovo's 'encrypted' fingerprint USB is just an unencrypted SD card in a case
Lenovo's 'encrypted' fingerprint USB drive is just an unencrypted SD card in a fancy case

editorial.brief: Lenovo's encrypted fingerprint USB drive turned out to be an unencrypted SD card in a fancy case, and both Hacker News and Lemmy noticed. On Wikipedia, Haley Stevens drew 360,148 views, 1.8 times the next article. Midterm odds and a magnitude 6.0 quake near Vanuatu filled most of the remaining space.
editorial.cover_sub: Haley Stevens took 360,148 views, well ahead of Patrick Stewart, while Polymarket priced Democratic control of the House at 95 percent and Google users in the US asked how to vote in the midterms.
editorial.wiki_deck: Haley Stevens led Wikipedia with 360,148 views, nearly double the runner-up. The snapshot offers a hint in its midterm-heavy feeds, though no source states the reason outright.
editorial.letter_headline: An ordinary Monday with one bad USB drive
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News builds video and book indexes of itself and frets over a late Postgres 19; Lemmy argues about Wheaton, daylight savings and RAM; Bluesky shares a lard cookbook and a woodpecker; Mastodon turns to art and voting.
editorial.foreign_deck: The largest of 25 quakes at M2.5 or above, a 6.0, hit 165 km NW of Port-Olry, Vanuatu, while Japan searched stockpile and emergency terms and India searched the Taiwan index.
editorial.markets_deck: Four of five markets are midterm bets: Democrats 95 percent for the House, Republicans 28 for the Senate. The outlier, a 1win token, trades at 100 percent on $4M.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 peaked at 1,288,020 players, with Dota 2 at 802,613 and PUBG at 802,207. Phantom Blade Zero reached 833,921. On Twitch, caseoh_ had 64,872 viewers, nearly four times summit1g's 16,366.
editorial.yt_note: Minecraft's Nether versus Overworld war leads with 2,856,276 views. Halloween and Christmas playlists share the list, the latter labelled 2027, along with an Avengers Doomsday teaser breakdown and a Fortnite One Piece trailer.
editorial.closing_note: By tomorrow's edition the Halloween playlist will have given way to the Christmas one, the Vanuatu quake will be a footnote, and Haley Stevens's 360,148 views will belong to someone else. The Lenovo drive will still be an SD card.
wiki_paras: Haley Stevens was the most-read article on Wikipedia in this snapshot, with 360,148 views. Patrick Stewart was second at 205,436, which puts the lead at 1.8 times the runner-up. Third place, .xxx, managed 197,312, so the real gap is between first and everyone else.

The data offers circumstantial help. One Mastodon post calls Haley Stevens an odd case and remarks on rats climbing onto a sinking ship, which suggests the argument is political. Meanwhile Google users in the US searched how to vote in the midterms, and prediction markets were busy with the same election.
